text:
Ana (PM): Quick sync — we need a rollout playbook for the "granular cutover ledger" feature (per-tenant routing + soft-degrade behavior). Customers have asked for opt-in, and infra needs clear guards. Looking for a short ops checklist: canary windows, A/B sizing, flag naming, fallback criteria, and comms. Can we sketch this here?

Sam (Eng): +1. Proposed high-level: 1) small canary (1% tenants) 2) expand to 5% then 25% with telemetry holds 3) wide rollout if green. Metrics to gate on: p95 latency, 5xx rate, unit cost delta, and model quality signal (eval set or automated QA).

Devon (SRE): Add capacity/queue checks. Specific triggers I'd suggest: auto-rollback if p95 latency increases > 20% relative to baseline OR 5xx rate increase > 0.5% absolute for 10m. Also kill-switch route that immediately routes traffic to fallback variant. We should have an emergency throttle per-region.

Sam (Eng): For A/B we should run a parity test for model outputs. Sampling config: 1% (30m), 5% (2h), 25% (24h). At each step we run a quick quality check against the core prompt set (n=200) with an automated regression detector. If quality regression > 2% we stop and rollback.

Kai (Product Ops): Naming + flag strategy idea: one top-level flag and subkeys per-tenant. Example: `feature.granular_cutover.{tenant_id}.strategy = {off|shadow|canary|full}`. Keep a global admin override. Please put that in the runbook.

Sam (Eng): Code snippet for the flag eval (for ops):

```
# pseudo
if flag.is_enabled(tenant):
  route_to_new_path()
else:
  route_to_current()
```

Devon (SRE): Telemetry/alerts: create a composite alert: (p95 > baseline *1.2) OR (error_rate > baseline + 0.005) OR (cost_per_request > baseline *1.15). Alert on both region and global. Dashboards: canary slice + shadow comparisons + per-tenant spike table.

Maria (CSE): For customers who opt-in: we need a comms template and an SLA note. Some enterprise customers want explicit windows and rollback promises. Suggest: 24h notice for opt-in, explicit escape hatch with immediate opt-out, and a post-rollout summary. I'll draft customer-facing text.

Kai (Product Ops): Runbook checkpoints: Preflight checklist (QA pass, infra capacity ok, telemetry baseline), Canary step, Hold/analysis, Expand, Postmortem. Who owns each step? We should capture time windows and required sign-offs.

Sam (Eng): Fallback variants: 1) Route to previous routing algorithm 2) Route to degraded mode (token cap, shorter responses) 3) Route to cached responses. Priority: preserve correctness > latency > cost.

Devon (SRE): Add automated evacuation policy: if we see sustained region pressure (GPU util > 85% for 10m) then start shedding new canary traffic from that region and reroute to fallback. Also ensure request tracing has a canary tag.

Ana (PM): Sounds good. Can we agree on specific numeric gates we all sign up to? My proposal: p95 increase tolerance 20%, 5xx increase tolerance 0.5% absolute, quality regression 2% on core set, cost per request increase 15%. If any hit, automatic hold and manual review.

Sam (Eng): Agree. Also add a softer warning threshold (e.g., p95 +10%) that triggers a proactive alert but doesn't hold rollout.

Maria (CSE): Who handles customer rollbacks? Ops or CSE? Suggest: Ops initiates technical rollback, CSE communicates to customer and coordinates follow-up.

Kai (Product Ops): I'll assemble the runbook and flag naming + gating matrix into a short doc. Action items: Kai draft runbook (today), Sam implement flag + metrics hooks (tomorrow), Devon add alerts + kill-switch (tomorrow), Maria draft customer comms (EOD).

deploy-bot: deploy triggered: `deploy/feature/granular-cutover v0.1 -> staging` :rocket:

Ana (PM): Thanks — put the runbook link here when ready. We'll use this thread as the single source for final signoffs. :thumbsup:
